question: Which statement best describes typeof guards?
options: typeof narrows primitive types. Inside if (typeof x === 'string'), TypeScript knows x is a string and lets you call string methods safely. It recognizes the JavaScript typeof results: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'symbol', 'bigint', 'undefined', 'object', and 'function'. It is the go-to guard for union types that mix primitives.

A plain truthiness check narrows away null, undefined, '', 0, and NaN. if (value) inside the block removes null | undefined from value's type, so you can safely access it. This is the idiomatic way to guard optional values before use, but beware that 0 and '' are also falsy.

in narrows by checking whether a property exists on an object. if ('swim' in animal) tells TypeScript animal is the member of the union that has a swim method. It is ideal for object unions that lack a shared discriminant but have distinguishing properties.

instanceof narrows to a class type by checking the prototype chain. Inside if (err instanceof TypeError), TypeScript treats err as a TypeError and exposes its members. Use it when discriminating between class instances — Error subclasses, Date, custom classes — rather than primitives.
